content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Does anyone know the structure of a digital input for a [product_name] programmable logic controller? The technical specifications mention there is no electrical isolation in the input. What does this actually imply? Best regards, [user_name]

When connecting your input sensor or switch, one side is linked to the same power supply as the [product_name]. If the input was electrically isolated, these circuits would be separated. Generally, this isn't a problem, but issues arise if you use the analog input (such as 0-10V/0-10mA) to measure a signal from a source with a different power supply than the [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to understand the internal configuration of digital inputs in [product_name] controllers, particularly the implication of no electrical isolation. While this is not usually a concern in routine scenarios, it can cause difficulties when measuring signals from supplies separate from the controller's own. The uncertainty is increased by insufficient technical documentation or diagrams for advanced setups.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a straightforward explanation of the internal circuit and clarification of 'no electrical isolation' for [product_name] digital inputs, especially with guidance for various practical applications.
